preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10^4) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(n, int) and 1 <= n <= 2 * 10**5 for n in [int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::3]])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first line after t is an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2*10^5) representing the number of elements in multisets a and b.

preconditions.expression: all(len(a) == n and len(b) == n for a, b, n in zip([list(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::3]], [list(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[3::3]], [int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::3]]))
preconditions.description: For each test case, the second and third lines contain exactly n integers each, representing the sorted (non-decreasing) elements of multisets a and b, respectively.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= 10**9 for x in sum([[int(x) for x in line.split()] for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::3]], []) + sum([[int(x) for x in line.split()] for line in stdin.splitlines()[3::3]], []))
preconditions.description: All elements in multisets a and b are integers between 1 and 10^9 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: all(stdout_line.strip() in ['YES', 'NO'] for stdout_line in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is either 'YES' or 'NO' (case-insensitive).
The number of output lines equals the number of test cases t.

postconditions.expression: all((lambda a, b: all(any((x == y) or (x % y == 0 and x // y == 2**k) or (y % x == 0 and y // x == 2**k) for k in range(0, 64)) for x, y in zip(sorted(a), sorted(b))) if len(a) == len(b) else False)(list(map(int, stdin.splitlines()[2 + 3*i].split())), list(map(int, stdin.splitlines()[3 + 3*i].split()))) == ('YES' == stdout.splitlines()[i].strip().upper()) for i in range(t))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is 'YES' if and only if there exists a way to transform multiset b into multiset a by doubling or halving (floor division) any element of b any number of times. This is determined by checking if the multisets a and b can be matched such that each element in a can be obtained from the corresponding element in b by a sequence of doubling or halving operations (i.e., x and y are in the same equivalence class where x = y * 2^k for some integer k).
